# Planetary Shields
While working on initial developments towards making planets more habitable, Horizon Energy initially concluded that some manner of preventing planetary landings was required.
Their chosen solution was the [italic]HZ-001 Planetary Shield Projection Device[/italic], more commonly known simply as the PSG or Planetary Shield Projector.
[color=gray][italic]A typical PSG.[/italic][/color]
The PSG is an incredibly high power device, drawing around [bold][color=red]2 gigawatts[/color][/bold] of power for operation. As such, a proper outpost capable of continually supplying that power is required, with an additional 500MW if the internal buffer needs recovering.
Additionally, the standard PSG has an energy buffer capable of lasting for around 2 minutes in order to prevent immediate shutoff. This also equates to requiring around 96 seconds to initially charge from a dead buffer at maximum power.
## Operation Guide
- Accumulate around 2GW of continual power, 2.5GW in case you need to recharge the buffer mid-operation. - Connect the PSG to high-voltage power cabling. - Wait around 96 seconds for the buffer to fully charge, and then another ~80 seconds to finish it's startup sequence. [bold][color=yellow]Do not allow the PSG to be destroyed during this time.[/color][/bold]
## Operation Notes - While online, the PSG projects a beam of pure energy out of the planet atmosphere in order to keep the shield stable. This beam is capable of [color=red]instantly annihilating[/color] anything that comes in contact with it. - The PSG prevents all ship landings while online. However, certain factions have manners of bypassing a shield, as described below.
## Bypassing
MMC, upon learning about Horizon's new shielding technology, took it upon themselves to find a way to at least stabily bypass this new generation of shields.
The primary weakness of these new hardlight shields is that they are weak to high speeds, which MMC chose to target with development of the Hellpod.
### Hellpods
[color=gray][italic]Looking at this makes you feel like screaming about freedom.[/italic][/color]
Hellpods are a quickly fabricated transport method for getting down to a point quickly. Importantly, the specific method of fabrication allows them to take an impact from a planetary shield and keep the occupant [italic]mostly[/italic] safe from the hit.
The primary method of using a Hellpod is to simply fabricate a boarding hatch on a ship and entering it on a planet; this will fire you directly downwards after around 3 seconds. The secondary method is through the use of a targetting console while in space in order to choose a specific place to drop down to planetside.
[color=gray][italic]A boarding hatch,[/italic][/color]
[color=gray][italic]and control console.[/italic][/color]
While using a control console, the map can be used to select a specific point on the planet map with the following controls:
- WASD moves the map with whatever your movement keybinds are set to. - Scrolling changes the map size; holding Control changes the drop area size. - Clicking on a location sets the console to drop to that place on the planet.
Preparing to launch pods requires a silo linked to a control console; there is no cost to firing pods on a planet, however. Once a launch location is locked in, all hatches will open and the required material shown on the left will be withdrawn to fabricate pods. Once all hatches have been entered, or after 30 seconds, a seperate 3 second countdown is started to prepare to fire the pods; after which, all occupied pods are fired down towards the area specified.
[bold]Importantly, if any pods breach a PSG, an alarm is blared over planetary Common, which will alert [color=red]EVERYONE on-planet[/color] that there are intruders.[/bold] Be ready for immediate resistance.
